On-Call Manager Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 June 2025. Replaces the single central on-call number with a regional on-call structure (three numbers, one per region).

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how staff contact an on-call manager outside of normal hours for a care-related concern requiring senior management input. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

Out of hours, staff call their own region's on-call mobile number (North West, Midlands or South West) — the previous single central number has been decommissioned — providing a reliable route to senior management support with a manager who knows the calling region well.

Definitions

**On-call manager** the senior manager currently holding the on-call rota responsibility for a specific region. **Regional on-call number** one of three mobile numbers, one per region, replacing the previous single central number. **Weekly rota** the rotation within each region's own senior management team, each taking on-call responsibility for one week at a time.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any staff member** on shift calls their own region's on-call number for a genuine out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input. **The regional on-call manager** answers their region's number during their rota week and provides guidance or attends site as the situation requires. **HR** maintains each region's weekly rota and ensures every senior manager knows their upcoming on-call weeks well in advance.

Call your own region's on-call mobile number for any out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input; the previous single central number has been decommissioned and no longer connects.

Give a clear, concise account of the situation to the regional on-call manager who answers, including what has already been done.

Follow the on-call manager's guidance, or arrange for them to attend site if they judge this necessary.

Record the call and its outcome in the site's on-call log.

Business Continuity Plan — Summary

Purpose and scope

This summary sets out how Alderbridge Care Group maintains critical care services during a major
disruption — severe weather, an IT outage, a utility failure, loss of a site, or a public health emergency. It
applies to every site and to Central Support Office, and is the top-level document under which each site's
own continuity annexe sits.

Policy statement

Alderbridge's continuity planning starts from the principle that personal care, medication administration and
safe staffing levels are non-negotiable critical services that must continue in any scenario; almost
everything else Alderbridge does can be paused, delayed or run in a reduced form if genuinely necessary.

Definitions

**Business continuity plan (BCP)** the documented arrangements for maintaining critical services during a
disruption. **Critical service** an activity whose interruption would create an immediate, serious risk to a
person supported. **Recovery time objective** the maximum acceptable time a service can be disrupted
before the impact becomes unacceptable. **Continuity annexe** a site-specific document providing the
operational detail (contact numbers, local resources, building-specific arrangements) this summary
deliberately does not repeat.

Roles and responsibilities

**The on-call director** may activate the BCP outside office hours and coordinates the immediate
response. **Each registered manager** maintains their own site's continuity annexe and is responsible for
its accuracy. **The Alderbridge Facilities Lead** coordinates any cross-site resource sharing (for example,
temporarily moving staff or equipment between sites) during an activated BCP. **IT** leads the technical
response to any system outage specifically.

Reviewing this plan's own effectiveness after a real incident

Following any genuine Tier 3 or Tier 4 incident, the Board reviews not only the specific incident's own handling but whether this plan itself, including the insurance notification step and Board co-approval requirement, held up as intended, distinct from the routine post-incident review IT leads.

Vendor and platform-specific considerations

Alderbridge's core systems span several different software vendors and hosting arrangements, each with its own incident notification process and support escalation route; IT maintains a current reference sheet of each vendor's own emergency contact and typical response time commitment, since assuming a generic response time across every vendor risks under- or over-estimating how quickly external support can realistically be engaged during a genuine incident.

Remote and home working considerations

A staff member who works remotely, such as a Central Support Office role, follows the same reporting standard as a site-based colleague, using their own approved device and secure connection; a remote worker's own home network is not treated as a controlled Alderbridge environment, and this plan's containment steps for a remote worker's device rely more heavily on remote isolation capability than the physical network disconnection available on site.

Closing note

A fast, coordinated response to a cyber incident protects resident data and care continuity, and the insurance notification and Board-level co-approval added in this version exist to make sure the most serious incidents also receive the financial and governance safeguards their consequence genuinely warrants.

Post-incident review process

Following any Tier 2 or higher incident, IT leads a post-incident review within 10 working days of resolution, completing the lessons-learned appendix template and documenting any change needed to this plan.

Detailed containment procedure by system type

Containment differs meaningfully depending on the affected system's nature. For a single endpoint device, IT disconnects it from the network immediately without powering it off, preserving volatile memory evidence. For a server-based system, IT isolates the affected network segment at the switch level rather than the individual server, since lateral spread may not yet be fully visible. For a cloud-hosted system, IT contacts the cloud provider's own security team in parallel with internal containment, since containment options there often require provider-side action.

Detailed containment procedure by system type (continued)

For a network device itself, IT does not simply power-cycle it, since this can both destroy evidence and, in some scenarios, trigger a malicious payload configured to activate on restart. For a shared care records system spanning multiple sites, IT considers whether a partial, site-by-site isolation is sufficient rather than isolating the entire system nationally, weighing containment benefit against operational disruption to unaffected sites.

Evidence preservation

Purpose and scope

Policy statement

A complaint alleging abuse, or involving a serious injury, bypasses the normal complaints timescale entirely and is escalated to the Quality Lead within 2 hours, reflecting the urgency this category of complaint genuinely warrants.

Definitions

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how staff respond to a power outage at any Alderbridge site. It applies to every shift, including night shifts when fewer staff are on duty.

Policy statement

A power outage is managed calmly, prioritising resident warmth, safety and medication integrity, while the wider Business Continuity Plan Summary is triggered if the outage is prolonged.

Definitions

Purpose and scope

This plan sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected cyber security incident, including ransomware, a data breach, or unauthorised system access. It applies to every site and every system holding Alderbridge or resident data.

Policy statement

A cyber incident is contained, reported and recovered from quickly and in a coordinated way, classified against the four-tier severity model, with the insurance and governance safeguards this version adds for the most serious incidents.

Definitions

Appendix: the two-stage test explained

This appendix explains the Act's own two-stage test in more practical detail. Stage one asks whether the person has an impairment or disturbance of the mind or brain, whether permanent or temporary — this alone does not determine incapacity, only whether the second stage needs to be considered at all. Stage two asks whether that impairment means the person cannot, at the time the decision needs to be made, understand relevant information about the decision, retain that information long enough to use it, weigh it up as part of the decision-making process, or communicate their decision by any means. A person lacks capacity for the specific decision only if stage one applies and they fail any one part of stage two — both stages genuinely matter, and staff are trained not to skip from 'has a diagnosis' straight to 'lacks capacity' without properly working through stage two.

For a decision that must be made urgently and there is no attorney or existing best interests decision in place, the treating professional or care team makes the decision in the person's best interests using the information available at that moment, records the reasoning fully as soon as practicable afterward, and reviews it with fuller information once the urgency has passed, since acting reasonably with incomplete information in a genuine emergency is preferable to delaying necessary care while a more complete process is followed.

Safe Administration of Medication Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group ensures medication is prescribed, ordered, stored, administered, recorded and reviewed safely and consistently across every site. It applies to every member of staff who has any contact with medication, from a registered nurse administering an injection to a housekeeping colleague who happens to find a dropped tablet on the floor. It does not cover community support workers assisting a person to self-administer under a documented capacity assessment — that specific activity is governed by the Self-Administration of Medication Policy, which this policy defers to entirely rather than duplicating.

Policy statement

Alderbridge Care Group believes that safe medication practice is one of the clearest, most measurable expressions of good care. Errors are treated as a system-level learning opportunity in the first instance, not automatically as individual misconduct, in line with the Medication Error Report Form's own no-blame first-response principle — although a pattern of repeated, avoidable error, or a single deliberately concealed error, is escalated through the Disciplinary Procedure.

Definitions

**MAR chart** the Medication Administration Record on which every dose given, refused, or omitted is signed for at the time of administration, never in advance and never retrospectively without a documented late-entry reason. **PRN medication** medication prescribed to be given only when required, subject to its own written PRN protocol describing the specific circumstances, maximum frequency and maximum daily dose. **Homely remedy** a limited over-the-counter remedy that may be given without an individual prescription, governed separately by the Homely Remedies Policy. **Competency assessment** the observed, signed-off assessment confirming a named member of staff is safe to administer medication unsupervised, distinct from simply having attended training. **Controlled drug** a medication subject to the additional legal controls and double-signing requirements set out separately in the Controlled Drugs Procedure.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how staff contact an on-call manager outside of normal hours for a care-related concern requiring senior management input. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

Out of hours, staff call their own region's on-call mobile number (North West, Midlands or South West) — the previous single central number has been decommissioned — providing a reliable route to senior management support with a manager who knows the calling region well.

Definitions

**On-call manager** the senior manager currently holding the on-call rota responsibility for a specific region. **Regional on-call number** one of three mobile numbers, one per region, replacing the previous single central number. **Weekly rota** the rotation within each region's own senior management team, each taking on-call responsibility for one week at a time.

Roles and responsibilities

Purpose and scope

Policy statement

Definitions

**Company-issued device** a phone or tablet provided by Alderbridge and enrolled in the mobile device management system before use. **Approved personal device** a staff member's own phone or tablet, approved by IT and enrolled in the same system, now used only under a bring-your-own-device arrangement for roles not accessing resident health records. **Enrolment** the process of registering a device in the mobile device management system, applying required security settings before it can access any Alderbridge system.

Roles and responsibilities

else) rather than searching for a script that does not exist for every possible scenario.

A worked example illustrates fast containment limiting a breach's impact. A member of staff at Central
Support Office emails a spreadsheet containing several employees' salary details to the wrong internal
distribution list. Realising the error within minutes, they immediately report it to the Data Protection Lead,

employees' rights and freedoms, and documents this assessment and reasoning, concluding it is not
independently notifiable to the ICO, though the affected employees are still told directly what happened as
a matter of transparency even though not legally required in this specific instance.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how staff contact an on-call manager outside of normal hours for a care-related concern requiring senior management input. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

Out of hours, staff call their own region's on-call mobile number (North West, Midlands or South West) — the previous single central number has been decommissioned — providing a reliable route to senior management support with a manager who knows the calling region well.

Definitions

**On-call manager** the senior manager currently holding the on-call rota responsibility for a specific region. **Regional on-call number** one of three mobile numbers, one per region, replacing the previous single central number. **Weekly rota** the rotation within each region's own senior management team, each taking on-call responsibility for one week at a time.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any staff member** on shift calls their own region's on-call number for a genuine out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input. **The regional on-call manager** answers their region's number during their rota week and provides guidance or attends site as the situation requires. **HR** maintains each region's weekly rota and ensures every senior manager knows their upcoming on-call weeks well in advance.

Call your own region's on-call mobile number for any out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input; the previous single central number has been decommissioned and no longer connects.

Give a clear, concise account of the situation to the regional on-call manager who answers, including what has already been done.

Follow the on-call manager's guidance, or arrange for them to attend site if they judge this necessary.

Record the call and its outcome in the site's on-call log.

treated as protecting Alderbridge's own credibility rather than a purely defensive regulatory formality.

A staff member who works remotely, such as a Central Support Office role, follows the same reporting standard as a site-based colleague, using their own approved device and secure connection; a remote worker's own home network is not treated as a controlled Alderbridge environment, and this plan's containment steps for a remote worker's device rely more heavily on remote isolation capability than the physical network disconnection available on site.

Post-incident review process

Following any Tier 2 or higher incident, IT leads a post-incident review within 10 working days of resolution, completing the lessons-learned appendix template and documenting any change needed to this plan.

Detailed containment procedure by system type

Containment differs meaningfully depending on the affected system's nature. For a single endpoint device, IT disconnects it from the network immediately without powering it off, preserving volatile memory evidence. For a server-based system, IT isolates the affected network segment at the switch level rather than the individual server, since lateral spread may not yet be fully visible. For a cloud-hosted system, IT contacts the cloud provider's own security team in parallel with internal containment, since containment options there often require provider-side action.

Detailed containment procedure by system type (continued)

For a network device itself, IT does not simply power-cycle it, since this can both destroy evidence and, in some scenarios, trigger a malicious payload configured to activate on restart. For a shared care records system spanning multiple sites, IT considers whether a partial, site-by-site isolation is sufficient rather than isolating the entire system nationally, weighing containment benefit against operational disruption to unaffected sites.

Evidence preservation

Before any remediation step that could alter or destroy evidence, IT takes a forensic image or detailed log export of the affected system where practicable, since a later insurance claim, regulatory enquiry, or law enforcement investigation may depend on evidence a hurried remediation step could otherwise destroy.

Communicating with residents and families during a cyber incident

Where a cyber incident genuinely affects a resident-facing system or resident data, the registered manager at an affected site is briefed by IT and, working with the Communications function, provides residents and families with a clear, honest, appropriately reassuring update, following the same honesty principle as the Duty of Candour Guidance, adapted to a cyber security context.

At Tier 3 or above, IT engages Alderbridge's retained external cyber security specialist firm, whose contact details and engagement terms are held centrally by IT and the cyber insurance provider, now formally coordinated with the insurance notification step this version introduces.

Serious Complaint Escalation Guidance

*Supersedes the version effective 1 July 2025. Escalation window tightened from 4 hours to 2 hours.*

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how a serious complaint is escalated at Alderbridge Care Group, distinct from the routine complaints timescale used for a general concern. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

A complaint alleging abuse, or involving a serious injury, bypasses the normal complaints timescale entirely and is escalated to the Quality Lead within 2 hours, reflecting the urgency this category of complaint genuinely warrants.

Definitions

**Serious complaint** a complaint alleging abuse, or involving a serious injury, as distinct from a general service concern handled under the routine complaints process. **Escalation window** the maximum time allowed between the complaint being received and the Quality Lead being informed, tightened in this version from 4 hours to 2 hours.

1. Identify whether a complaint meets the serious complaint threshold as soon as it is received, escalating an unclear case rather than defaulting to the routine timescale.
2. Escalate a serious complaint to the Quality Lead within 2 hours of it being received, a tightening from the previous 4-hour window, regardless of the time of day.
3. Continue to acknowledge the complainant promptly using the routine complaints process's normal courtesy steps, alongside the separate urgent escalation.
4. Record the time the complaint was received and the time it was escalated, supporting a clear audit of whether the 2-hour window was met.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Adult Safeguarding Policy (a serious complaint alleging abuse is also a safeguarding concern) and the CQC Notification Procedure (relevant where the underlying event is also notifiable).

Worked example

Lead puts interim measures
in place immediately where a plausible, proportionate one exists — for example, temporarily suspending a
specific system's remote access pending confirmation of how a credential was compromised — rather
than waiting for the complete investigation to conclude before taking any protective action at all.

Post-breach review and organisational learning

Beyond the individual breach's own resolution, the Data Protection Lead reviews breach data quarterly for
any recurring type or cause, and a genuinely recurring pattern (for example, repeated misdirected emails
to a similarly named recipient) triggers a specific process or system change — for example, a mandatory
confirmation step before sending to an external address — rather than each individual recurrence simply
being logged and closed without addressing why it keeps happening.

Distinguishing a breach from an ordinary IT fault

Not every IT problem is a data breach; a system outage that prevents access to data, with no evidence
anyone unauthorised accessed or exfiltrated it, is handled under the IT Outage Contact Tree rather than
this procedure, though the Data Protection Lead is still briefed and remains alert to any sign the outage's
underlying cause might also have a data protection dimension that only becomes apparent as IT's own
investigation progresses.

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how staff respond to a power outage at any Alderbridge site. It applies to every shift, including night shifts when fewer staff are on duty.

Policy statement

A power outage is managed calmly, prioritising resident warmth, safety and medication integrity, while the wider Business Continuity Plan Summary is triggered if the outage is prolonged.

Definitions

Policy statement

Definitions

**Cyber incident** any suspected compromise of an Alderbridge system. **Containment** the immediate step of isolating an affected system to prevent further spread. **The Data Protection Officer (DPO)** assesses personal data breach implications within 12 hours. **Severity tier** one of four classifications (Tier 1 to Tier 4). **Cyber insurance provider notification** the new mandatory step, introduced in this version, notifying Alderbridge's cyber insurance provider at Tier 3 or above. **Board Chair co-approval** the new requirement, introduced in this version, for a Tier 4 ransomware-related decision.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the immutable backup's purpose. During a simulated ransomware exercise,
IT finds that standard, writable backups from the preceding week would themselves have been encrypted
alongside the primary system in a genuine attack of this type; the immutable, air-gapped copy remains
untouched and unencrypted, providing the actual recovery source the exercise confirms would be needed
in that scenario.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was an immutable backup added when the 3-2-1 principle already existed?** A review found that a
sophisticated ransomware attack can specifically target and encrypt a standard backup alongside the
primary system if both are reachable from the same compromised network; an immutable, air-gapped copy
cannot be altered even in that scenario. **What is the difference between RTO and RPO?** RTO is how
quickly a system is restored; RPO is how much data loss, measured in time, is acceptable — a
nightly-backed-up system has an RPO of roughly 24 hours since up to a day's data could be lost if the
incident occurs just before that night's backup.

Training and competency

IT staff complete training on immutable backup management and the distinction between RTO and RPO,
building on the existing monthly test restoration training.

Monitoring and compliance

The IT Director reviews backup completion, test restoration outcomes and immutable backup integrity
monthly, reporting to the Board quarterly.

Record keeping and retention

Backup completion logs, test restoration outcomes, and documented RTOs and RPOs are retained per the
Records Retention Schedule.

Appendix: the two-stage test explained

This appendix explains the Act's own two-stage test in more practical detail. Stage one asks whether the person has an impairment or disturbance of the mind or brain, whether permanent or temporary — this alone does not determine incapacity, only whether the second stage needs to be considered at all. Stage two asks whether that impairment means the person cannot, at the time the decision needs to be made, understand relevant information about the decision, retain that information long enough to use it, weigh it up as part of the decision-making process, or communicate their decision by any means. A person lacks capacity for the specific decision only if stage one applies and they fail any one part of stage two — both stages genuinely matter, and staff are trained not to skip from 'has a diagnosis' straight to 'lacks capacity' without properly working through stage two.

Working with family members who hold Lasting Power of Attorney

Where a family member holds a registered Lasting Power of Attorney for health and welfare, or for property and financial affairs, staff confirm the specific scope of that authority before relying on it, since an attorney's authority is decision-specific to the type of LPA registered and does not automatically extend to every decision about the person, and Alderbridge keeps a copy of the registered document on file rather than relying on the family member's own description of their authority.

When a decision genuinely cannot wait

For a decision that must be made urgently and there is no attorney or existing best interests decision in place, the treating professional or care team makes the decision in the person's best interests using the information available at that moment, records the reasoning fully as soon as practicable afterward, and reviews it with fuller information once the urgency has passed, since acting reasonably with incomplete information in a genuine emergency is preferable to delaying necessary care while a more complete process is followed.

Safe Administration of Medication Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group ensures medication is prescribed, ordered, stored, administered, recorded and reviewed safely and consistently across every site. It applies to every member of staff who has any contact with medication, from a registered nurse administering an injection to a housekeeping colleague who happens to find a dropped tablet on the floor. It does not cover community support workers assisting a person to self-administer under a documented capacity assessment — that specific activity is governed by the Self-Administration of Medication Policy, which this policy defers to entirely rather than duplicating.

Policy statement

Alderbridge Care Group believes that safe medication practice is one of the clearest, most measurable expressions of good care. Errors are treated as a system-level learning opportunity in the first instance, not automatically as individual misconduct, in line with the Medication Error Report Form's own no-blame first-response principle — although a pattern of repeated, avoidable error, or a single deliberately concealed error, is escalated through the Disciplinary Procedure.

Definitions

**MAR chart** the Medication Administration Record on which every dose given, refused, or omitted is signed for at the time of administration, never in advance and never retrospectively without a documented late-entry reason. **PRN medication** medication prescribed to be given only when required, subject to its own written PRN protocol describing the specific circumstances, maximum frequency and maximum daily dose. **Homely remedy** a limited over-the-counter remedy that may be given without an individual prescription, governed separately by the Homely Remedies Policy. **Competency assessment** the observed, signed-off assessment confirming a named member of staff is safe to administer medication unsupervised, distinct from simply having attended training. **Controlled drug** a medication subject to the additional legal controls and double-signing requirements set out separately in the Controlled Drugs Procedure.

Policy statement

Definitions

*Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2024. Withdraws the bring-your-own-device allowance for roles accessing resident health records; those roles now require a company-issued device only.*

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group manages mobile devices, including phones and tablets used to access resident records or care systems. It applies to every company-issued device and, for roles not accessing resident health records, every personal device approved for work use.

Policy statement

A mobile device that can access resident information is managed to the same security standard as an office computer, and for roles accessing resident health records specifically, only a company-issued device is now used, so that resident data remains protected wherever it is accessed from.

Definitions

**Company-issued device** a phone or tablet provided by Alderbridge and enrolled in the mobile device management system before use. **Approved personal device** a staff member's own phone or tablet, approved by IT and enrolled in the same system, now used only under a bring-your-own-device arrangement for roles not accessing resident health records. **Enrolment** the process of registering a device in the mobile device management system, applying required security settings before it can access any Alderbridge system.

Roles and responsibilities

**IT** enrols every device, company-issued or approved personal, before it is permitted to access any Alderbridge system, confirms which roles require a company-issued device under this version, and can remotely wipe a lost or stolen device. **The device user** reports a lost or stolen device to IT immediately and never disables the security settings the enrolment process applies. **The registered manager** approves which staff roles require mobile access to resident systems at their site and confirms which of those roles now require a company-issued device.

Purpose and scope

Policy statement

A mobile device that can access resident information is managed to the same security standard as an office computer, and for roles accessing resident health records specifically, only a company-issued device is now used, so that resident data remains protected wherever it is accessed from.

Definitions

Roles and responsibilities

On-Call Manager Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 June 2025. Replaces the single central on-call number with a regional on-call structure (three numbers, one per region).

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how staff contact an on-call manager outside of normal hours for a care-related concern requiring senior management input. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

Out of hours, staff call their own region's on-call mobile number (North West, Midlands or South West) — the previous single central number has been decommissioned — providing a reliable route to senior management support with a manager who knows the calling region well.

Definitions

**On-call manager** the senior manager currently holding the on-call rota responsibility for a specific region. **Regional on-call number** one of three mobile numbers, one per region, replacing the previous single central number. **Weekly rota** the rotation within each region's own senior management team, each taking on-call responsibility for one week at a time.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any staff member** on shift calls their own region's on-call number for a genuine out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input. **The regional on-call manager** answers their region's number during their rota week and provides guidance or attends site as the situation requires. **HR** maintains each region's weekly rota and ensures every senior manager knows their upcoming on-call weeks well in advance.

Call your own region's on-call mobile number for any out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input; the previous single central number has been decommissioned and no longer connects.

Give a clear, concise account of the situation to the regional on-call manager who answers, including what has already been done.

Follow the on-call manager's guidance, or arrange for them to attend site if they judge this necessary.

Record the call and its outcome in the site's on-call log.

Insurance and financial continuity

Alderbridge maintains business interruption insurance covering the financial impact of an extended site
closure, reviewed annually by the Finance function alongside this summary, so that a major disruption's
financial consequences do not themselves become a second crisis compounding the operational one; the
specific policy terms and claims process are held by Finance rather than repeated in this operationally
focused summary.

Testing the plan beyond the annual desktop exercise

In addition to the annual desktop exercise referenced above, Alderbridge runs at least one unannounced,
limited-scope continuity test each year at a rotating site — for example, testing the generator's actual load
capacity rather than only its ability to start, or testing whether the local staff contact tree numbers are
genuinely current — since a plan that has only ever been reviewed on paper can contain errors (an
outdated phone number, an assumption about equipment capacity) that only a genuine test, however
limited in scope, would reveal.

Mutual aid arrangements with other local care providers

Alderbridge maintains an informal mutual aid understanding with two other local care providers in each
region, allowing for emergency short-term support (for example, temporary bed space for an evacuated
resident, or borrowed equipment) during a disruption severe enough to exceed Alderbridge's own internal
cross-site resource-sharing capacity; this arrangement is reviewed annually to confirm it remains current
and is never assumed to still be in place without that yearly reconfirmation.

Communicating with the local authority and CQC during an activation

Where a BCP activation is significant enough to affect service delivery in a way a regulator or
commissioner would reasonably expect to be told about, the registered manager notifies the local authority
and, where the CQC notification threshold under the CQC Notification Procedure is met, the CQC,
proactively rather than waiting to be asked, since early, honest communication during a genuine crisis is
treated as protecting Alderbridge's own credibility rather than a purely defensive regulatory formality.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where the regional on-call manager does not answer within a reasonable number of attempts, staff proceed with whatever immediate action resident safety requires (such as calling emergency services) without waiting further, and may also try a neighbouring region's number as a fallback, then report the missed contact to HR the following working day.

Local and regional variations

Each region now has its own dedicated on-call number and rota; a site calls its own region's number as standard, using a neighbouring region's number only as the fallback described above.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This procedure works alongside the Key Holder Procedure (a separate, parallel escalation route for a site security or alarm concern) and the Adult Safeguarding Policy (relevant where the on-call concern is itself a safeguarding matter).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the regional standard. A shift lead at a South West site needs senior management input following an unusual overnight incident. They call the South West on-call number directly, reaching a manager who knows the region's specific context, sites and relationships well, a difference from the previous version where the answering manager might have had no prior familiarity with that region at all.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was the single central number replaced with regional numbers?** A review found staff valued speaking to a manager who knew their specific region's context; regional numbers make that familiarity the norm rather than a matter of chance. **What happens if a staff member accidentally still has the old central number saved?** It has been fully decommissioned and will not connect; site noticeboards and induction materials were updated with the new regional numbers ahead of the change.

Training and competency

A senior manager joining a region's on-call rota completes an on-call induction covering common scenario types and the escalation options available to them, including the new fallback-to-neighbouring-region process.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where immediate containment requires an action outside a member of staff's normal authority (for
example, isolating a shared system that other staff are actively using), the decision is escalated to IT or the
Data Protection Lead immediately rather than a member of staff acting unilaterally beyond their role,
except where the delay itself would clearly make the breach significantly worse.

Local and regional variations

No local or regional variation applies; breach reporting and the 1-hour internal escalation window are
identical across every site and Central Support Office, reflecting the same 72-hour regulatory clock
applying regardless of where a breach occurs.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This procedure sits underneath the Data Protection Policy's general framework, and works alongside the
Cyber Incident Response Plan for a breach with a technical cyber cause, and the CCTV Policy and
Records Retention Schedule for breaches specific to those processing activities.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates fast containment limiting a breach's impact. A member of staff at Central
Support Office emails a spreadsheet containing several employees' salary details to the wrong internal
distribution list. Realising the error within minutes, they immediately report it to the Data Protection Lead,
who recalls the email where technically possible and contacts every recipient directly asking them to delete
it unopened, confirming compliance from each. The Data Protection Lead assesses the breach, given the
swift containment and the limited, internal-only recipient list, as unlikely to result in a risk to the affected
employees' rights and freedoms, and documents this assessment and reasoning, concluding it is not
independently notifiable to the ICO, though the affected employees are still told directly what happened as
a matter of transparency even though not legally required in this specific instance.

constitute a financial concern requiring Safeguarding Lead escalation.
